title: What REALLY Happens When Electricity Goes Through Your Body?
sources: OSHA: 100 mA through the heart causes ventricular fibrillation — the heart quivers instead of pumping
Electrical burns appear small externally but destroy tissue along the entire current path internally
Electrocution physics: human body resistance 1000-2000 ohms; 120V household current can push 60-120 mA through the chest — lethal range
NEJM: lightning strike survivors often survive because the current is so brief it causes cardiac arrest then restarts the heart

lines.text: When electricity enters your body, it looks for the fastest path to ground.
lines.caps: When *electricity | enters your body | fastest *path | to *ground

lines.text: That path runs straight through your heart.
Just sixty milliamps — the power of a small light bulb — is enough to kill you.
The current hijacks your nervous system and locks every muscle in your body.
You cannot let go of the wire.
Your heart begins fibrillating — quivering instead of pumping.
Internally, the current has scorched a path through your organs.
Lightning does the opposite — the bolt is so brief your heart stops then restarts.
That is why lightning strike survivors can walk away.
But a household socket holds on long enough to end you.
